## Main result

{"rewarding": "Insufficient to sustain contributions on its own, but part of a synergistic relationship with sanctioning.", "sanctioning": "Sustains public goods provision at a level above that observed in the absence of sanctioning opportunities."}

## What they prove

The effectiveness of sanctions and rewards in maintaining contributions to public goods.

## What they only simulate

None

## What they do NOT test

None

## What we need to reproduce

The results of this study should be reproduced in other contexts to further understand the impact of sanctions and rewards on public goods provision.

## How our project differs

This project differs from previous studies by introducing opportunities for both rewarding and sanctioning in a single stage game.
